{{Quote|I want a ''Rogue''-class starfighter with elite weapons, cloaking device, the works.|Cad Bane, to Darth Sidious|<ref name="Holocron Heist" />}}
The '''''Rogue''-class Porax-38 starfighter''', also known simply as the '''''Rogue''-class starfighter''', '''Porax-38 starfighter''', or '''P-38 fighter''', was a model of [[starfighter]] manufactured by [[Baktoid Armor Workshop]] and [[Buuper Torsckil Abbey Devices]] and used by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. Often flown by specially programmed [[IG-100 MagnaGuard]]s, it came to informally be known as the '''MagnaGuard Fighter'''. The [[bounty hunter]] [[Cad Bane]] owned a modified ''Rogue''-class starfighter known as the ''[[Xanadu Blood]]''.

==Characteristics==
[[File:Magnaguard-fighter.png|thumb|left|300px|A MagnaGuard piloting a ''Rogue''-class starfighter]]
Manufactured by both [[Baktoid Armor Workshop]]<ref name="Updated and Expanded" /> and [[Buuper Torsckil Abbey Devices]],<ref name="Complete Vehicles" /> the ''Rogue''-class fighter was a bigger [[starfighter]] with a bulbous [[cockpit]] and heavy [[laser cannon]]s on both wings. It measured 12.7 [[meter]]s in length.<ref name="MagnaGuard Fighter" /> It shared its name with the [[Porax-28 starfighter]].<ref name="The Glass Abyss">''[[Mace Windu: The Glass Abyss]]''</ref>

==History==
''Rogue''-class starfighters were used by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars]].<ref name="The Clone Wars film" /> They were often flown by specially programmed [[IG-100 MagnaGuard]], though they were also [[pilot]]ed by Separatist leaders and hirelings.<ref name="MagnaGuard Fighter" /> During [[Count]] [[Dooku]]'s failed plot to secure access to [[Hutt Space]] during the Clone Wars, he had two of his MagnaGuards fly ''Rogue''-class starfighters. Though the fighters were destroyed, they were successful in shooting down his arch-nemesis Jedi General [[Anakin Skywalker]]’s ship, the ''[[Twilight]]''.<ref name="The Clone Wars film" /> During the [[Battle of Abrion Bridge]], Separatist-led units were used to destroy Skywalker’s [[Jedi Master|Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]'s [[212th Attack Battalion|forces]].<ref name="Obi-Wan 3">[[Obi-Wan 3|''Obi-Wan'' 3]]</ref>  Several of these ''Rogue''-class starfighters were stored aboard [[Skytop Station]] prior to its destruction, likely for defense. All starfighters, including the ''Rogue''-class, aboard, were destroyed with the rest of the station. Although [[General]] [[Grievous]] managed to escape the station aboard his personal starfighter, ''[[Soulless One]]''.<ref name="DOTD">{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}}</ref>

The bounty hunter [[Durge]] also piloted a ''Rogue''-class starfighter over a [[Color|green]] astronomical object when he worked with the Confederacy.<ref name="Transmissions">{{AtomicMassGames|url=transmission/hot-shots-aces-ii-separatist-overview|text=Hot Shots and Aces II Separatist Overview|date=2022-11-22}}</ref>

[[File:CadBaneScum-SWZ92.png|thumb|left|300px|Cad Bane pilots his ''Rogue''-class fighter ''Xanadu Blood'' away from Jabba's palace]]
[[Cad Bane]] was then given a fighter, the ''[[Xanadu Blood]]'', by his [[Sith Lord]] client and Dooku's Master [[Darth Sidious]] equipped with elite weapons and a [[cloaking device]] as part of his payment for stealing a [[Jedi holocron]] along with his usual payment times three.<ref name="Holocron Heist" /> Bane used his ''Rogue''-class starfighter to kidnap two [[Force-sensitive]] children; [[Wee Dunn]] and [[Zinn Toa]], from [[Rodia]] and [[Glee Anselm]] and took them to [[Mustafar]]. Bane and his ship were captured by Skywalker and his [[Ahsoka Tano|apprentice]] on [[Naboo]]. Onboard the ''[[Resolute]]'', Skywalker and Tano searched his ship but his [[Navigation computer|navigation logs]] were wiped, eventually discovering that he also went to Mustafar due to his ship collecting a lot of ashes and checking his [[fuel computer]].<ref name="Children of the Force" />

At some point, Bane was able to reclaim his fighter, using it during his work for the Hutts.<ref name="Evil Plans">{{TCW|Evil Plans}}</ref> Bane and his [[techno-service droid]] [[Todo 360]], then used it to track [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure|Ziro]] to his [[Papa|father's]] grave on [[Teth]]. Bane and Todo manage to escape [[Quinlan Vos]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] using the starfighter.<ref name="Hunt for Ziro" /> At some point, Bane replaced the ''Xanadu Blood'' with a new ship, the ''[[Justifier]]''.<ref name="Bounty Lost Trivia">{{SW|url=bounty-lost-trivia-gallery|text=Tech's Notes: "Bounty Lost" Trivia Gallery}}</ref>

''Rogue''-class starfighters were also used on [[Utapau]] by the [[Utapau Skyforce]]. Near the end of the Clone Wars, the skyforce allied with the Republic and engaged the Droid Army in the [[Battle of Utapau]].<ref name="Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Fighter_Concept.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Concept art of what would become the ''Rogue''-class starfighter, by [[Ryan Church]].]]
The ''Rogue''-class Porax-38 starfighter was originally created for the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars:'' Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']].<ref name="Revenge of the Sith" />

It was a late addition to the film and, though a digital model was created for the starfighter, it was never completed to the level originally planned.<ref name="P-38 starfighter">{{DB|starship|p38starfighter|P-38 starfighter}}</ref>

The P-38 fighter was inspired by the real-world [[Wikipedia:Lockheed P-38 Lightning|Lockheed P-38 Lightning]], a World War II fighter aircraft. It shares a number of characteristics with the P-38 Lightning, including a pair of twin tails and similar engine scoops.<ref name="WIRED">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@WIRED|name=WIRED|link=Wikipedia:Wired (magazine)|video=LPPLCkIhxt0|text=Every Starfighter in Star Wars Explained By Lucasfilm}}</ref>

A [[gunship]] bearing a strong resemblance to the ''Rogue''-class appeared in "[[Chapter 6: The Prisoner]]," an episode from the [[2019]] [[Disney+]] television series, ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]''. Concept art showcased in the episode's credits depicted the ship as appearing closer to a stock ''Rogue''-class than in the final episode.<ref name="Chapter 6">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 6: The Prisoner}}</ref> ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Handbook]]'' established that [[Ranzar Malk]] owned an upgraded ''Rogue''-class Porax-38 starfighter.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Handbook]]''</ref> ''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]'' established this craft to be the [[Rogue-class Gunship|''Rogue''-class Gunship]].<ref name="Outlaws">''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]''</ref>
